items.title: Charles Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, August 23, 1997
items.q: if you’re speaking about Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and Thelonious Monk, there’s nothing like it.

ctx.x: Do you consider jazz to be, some people call it America’s classical music, or black classical music. Do you have a sense of how jazz is — your own personal sense of how jazz should be viewed?

It should be viewed with great respect. Myself personally, you know that’s my personal opinion. Because there’s nothing like it. I mean speaking of jazz, if you’re speaking about Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker and Thelonious Monk, there’s nothing like it. It’s such a heck of a creative venue that nothing’s been created since then to equal it. It’s output, musically and emotionally and spiritually.
Why do you think jazz, when it moved into the bebop era, that it lost a good portion of its audience?
